Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second innings. Jos Buttler and Phil Salt stride out to open for England. It will be Akeal Hosein to start the proceedings with the ball for West Indies. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Another lackluster outing with the ball for England as they couldn't capitalize on the early breakthroughs. Adil Rashid and Sam Curran snapped 4 wickets among them while Topley and Moeen Ali chipped in with one each. Mills, Livingstone, and Atkinson were peppered for 96 runs in their 6 overs combined as the Windies batters bludgeoned them all around the park. The target is a stiff one and the English batters will need to be on top gear right from ball one. Can they chase this down and stay alive in the series? We shall find out. Join us for the second essay in a while from now.

The star with the bat for West Indies, Nicholas Pooran is down for a chat. He says he had proper game plans in mind for this match and was disappointed of his dismissal with 2 more overs in hand. He adds that he is pleased with the score on board and that his partnership after the initial wickets was important and he backs himself to play according to situations.

Wow! What a finish! Another six-hitting run fest by the West Indies batters powers them to 222 in their allotted 20 overs. Having put into bat first, England picked up two early wickets and sent both the openers back into the hut. Pooran and Hope steadied the innings with a 54-run stand before Hope departed in the quest to up the ante. Skipper Rovman Powell joined Pooran in the middle and the duo started nailing boundaries right from the word go. Powell smacked a 21-ball 39 while Pooran played an outstanding knock of 82. Rutherford, Russell, and Holder, all played their part to take the Men in Maroon to the highest score at this venue.

SIX! 6, 4 and 6 to finish things off by Jason Holder! Hard length outside off, trying to angle it away, Holder moves past the off stump before reaching out and powering it over the cover fence for a biggie. West Indies have once again hit more maximums than fours in their innings and end with 'double nelson' (222) for 6!

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break! After a couple of early setbacks, West Indies have done really well to get into a position of promise. Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin. The umpires are out in the middle and so are the West Indies opening pair of Brandon King and Kyle Mayers. The players of England also stride out to the middle. It will be the off-spin of Moeen Ali to get things underway yet again for England. Let's play....

Tymal Mills is now down for a chat as well. He says he's happy to be back in the squad and with the World Cup coming in and the competitions for the available slots in this team, he is looking forward to putting his right foot here in this game and getting back to consistency. He explains his naturally developed 'Back of the hand slower ball' that he has been bowling for so long now and looks forward to executing them in the game today depending on how the surface behaves.

Akeal Hosein is down for a quick chat before the game. He says that it has been fantastic so far, the support and the camaraderie as well and winning certainly helps. Adds that being a spinner in the Powerplay, you have to execute well but you need to have that clarity no matter which batter is on strike. Mentions that it is always best to have a plan from the start and if you stick to your plan, it is the batter that has to adjust.

PITCH REPORT - Samuel Badree is pitchside. He says that it is the same surface from the last game but the stark difference is that it is much drier and will play better than the last game. Adds that this is one of the highest-scoring venues in West Indies and the last game shows that you can target a bowler and score big in one over but there will be something in it for the spinners as well.

Rovman Powell, the Windies skipper says that they would have chased as well but the wicket looks even better than the last game. Adds that last time it started a bit tacky but got better as the game went on. Adds that they need to continue to build partnerships and if they don't lose wickets, they can fire later on. Informs that Sherfane Rutherford comes in for Shimron Hetmyer. Ends by saying that winning the series would be a big deal as they haven't been able to notch up a series win against this opposition for a long time.

Jos Buttler, the captain of England says that they will bowl first and adds that they need to make a few tweaks on the key areas they missed in the previous game and conceded 10-15 more runs that cost them the match. He explains how important the execution is, both with the bat and ball keeping in mind it is just 20 overs game and every delivery will be crucial. He concludes by informing about the two changes with Gus Atkinson and Reece Topley coming in for Chris Woakes and Rehan Ahmed.

England (Playing XI) - Jos Buttler (C/WK), Phil Salt, Will Jacks, Liam Livingstone, Harry Brook, Moeen Ali, Sam Curran, Gus Atkinson (In for Chris Woakes), Adil Rashid, Reece Topley (In for Rehan Ahmed), Tymal Mills.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Kyle Mayers, Shai Hope, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Sherfane Rutherford (In for Shimron Hetmyer), Rovman Powell (C), Gudakesh Motie, Andre Russell, Jason Holder, Akeal Hosein, Alzarri Joseph.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favor of Jos Buttler and England will BOWL first.

England, on the other hand, haven’t been at their best for quite some time. They lost the ODI series and are already behind in the T20Is. They were restricted to 166 and lost the second game by 10 runs. Sam Curran had a good outing with the bat but the rest of the batters got starts and failed to get going. Adil Rashid and Tymal Mills were outstanding with the ball. England will need to step up as a unit if they are to make a comeback and avoid another series loss. Can England get back to winning ways and stop West Indies from taking the series? We shall find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit. Stay tuned!

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the 3rd T20I between England and West Indies in this 5-match series from the National Cricket Stadium in Grenada. West Indies have won the first two games and will want to take the series with a win today. In the second game of the T20 series, West Indies posted a competitive score of 176 after batting first. Brandon King was the top scorer with a sublime 82 while skipper Rovman Powell also made a fine fifty. The bowlers followed it up nicely and the Men in Maroon came out on top by just 10 runs in a close game. Alzarri Joseph with a three-fer and Akeal Hosein with 2 for 24 were key to defending the total. West Indies are coming off two excellent wins and clinching the series against the World Champions will make it better for them.
…MATCHDAY…

England's white-ball tour of West Indies is nearing its end but there are still three electrifying T20Is to go. National Cricket Stadium, St George's in Grenada will play host to the 2nd T20I between West Indies and England just as it did in the 2nd T20I and it is do-or-die territory from here for England. Having lost the three-match ODI series 2-1, the visitors came into the five-match T20I series with a lot of hope just as they should have as well being the reigning T20I champions of the World but things have not gone according to plan for them. The hosts defeated them comfortably in the 1st ODI by 4 wickets and then in a much-narrowly fought encounter in the 2nd T20I, England still couldn't get over the line and lost the game by 10 runs. Skipper, Jos Buttler continues to battle with his own form which has been very up and down throughout the last few months and having too many top-order batters in the lineup isn't quite working out for them. Sam Curran though did a fine job batting at number 3 in the last game but they need to have some sort of solidity in that middle order. As far as the bowling is concerned, it has been decent but they have let the opposition off the hook after having them cornered which they will hope not to repeat. Speaking about the hosts, West Indies, they seem to have found a bit of their mojo back and with big names like Andre Russell, Nicholas Pooran and Rovman Powell all coming off some great performances in franchise cricket, they have been able to translate some of that form to international cricket as well. Brandon King though was the star of the last game and along with Powell took his team to a solid total. The bowling too seems to be coming together with the spin duo of Akeal Hosein and Gudakesh Motie doing a stellar job and Alzarri Joseph closing out games but they would look to find an extra bowling option as Andre Russell was pummeled in the last game. Can England manage to cut the deficit in half and keep the series alive? Or will West Indies round off a 3-0 series win with two games in hand? We shall find out.
